card.title: TYPHOON Mk IB
card.text: When a ground unit retreats, draw a card.
card.flavorText: The Hawker Typhoon, also nicknamed Tiffy by RAF pilots, was a British fighter-bomber produced by Hawker Aircraft. It was originally intended as a medium to high altitude interceptor, but it never took on that role due to several design problems. When the Typhoon came into service in 1941 it was the only aircraft that could catch up with the German Focke-Wulf and as a result it took on a role as a low-altitude interceptor. Later it established itself as a night time intruder and long-range fighter. From 1942 to 1943 bombs and later RP-3 rockets were added to its arsenal, and along with its 4 x 20mm Hispano autocannons it became the most powerful ground-attack aircraft of WWII.
